Ensure incoming connections wait for executing server calls before freeing node state

why: P2 because it fixes a crash during node shutdown when asynchronous IPC calls are active
Hardens connection teardown and crash handling for external processes using the IPC mining interface

result.summary: This PR modifies `Ipc::disconnectIncoming` and libmultiprocess connection handling so that disconnecting incoming IPC clients waits for in-flight server method bodies to finish executing before node state is destroyed. It introduces a `ServerObjectTracker` and `Connection::waitDrained()` to ensure asynchronous calls running on worker threads finish before shutdown proceeds to reset node subsystems.
result.problem: During node shutdown, disconnecting incoming IPC clients cancels KJ promises but does not halt C++ server method bodies already dispatched to worker threads. A running call (such as `Mining.checkBlock`) can dereference `m_node.chainman` after shutdown has reset it, triggering an assertion failure (#35845, #33387).

result.card: This PR updates libmultiprocess and IPC connection teardown to wait for in-progress asynchronous IPC calls to drain before incoming connections are destroyed during shutdown. It fixes an assertion failure in MinerImpl::chainman() where asynchronous mining calls dereference node state after Shutdown() has already freed it (#35845, #33387). The PR is currently marked as a draft and depends on upstream libmultiprocess PR 335, with failing CI and no reviewer activity yet.
